machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.1:ב: (ב) Since some say even an adult, etc., fulfills through this kiddush, etc. — this is the position of Sir Mitzuta that Mordechai brought. However these three words "fulfills through this kiddush" appear neither in Mordechai nor in the great Beit Yosef who copied him; and the essence of Mordechai's words in his name is as Rav said: those elders who made kiddush in the synagogue — their obligation of kiddush was fulfilled but their obligation of wine was not fulfilled; meaning when they come home and drink at home they must repeat and bless, for change of place constitutes an interruption. And Shmuel said: even their obligation of kiddush was not fulfilled, for kiddush is only in the place of a meal. And since Rav said their obligation of wine was not fulfilled, and Shmuel too said even obligation of kiddush was not fulfilled — implying all the more obligation of wine was not fulfilled. And if one thought they did not drink in the synagogue from the wine it is obvious; how could one think their obligation of wine was fulfilled — behold that is an interruption between blessing and tasting. Rather it must refer to drinking in the synagogue from the cup. And for Shmuel how is drinking in the synagogue permitted — behold kiddush is only in the place of a meal? Rather drinking is permitted — so is the halacha. And therefore the intent is not that they fulfilled obligation of kiddush by what they sanctified in the synagogue — for Shmuel said explicitly obligation of kiddush was not fulfilled, etc. Rather meaning they fulfill through this kiddush for the matter of permission to drink, which is lighter than eating. And so I found in Sefer Or Zarua who brought in the name of Rashba that one may drink before kiddush, for they forbade only eating before kiddush and not drinking — behold he holds drinking is lighter than eating; so too one may say according to Sir Mitzuta per his method. And Bach wrote they give specifically to minors who have not reached education; and one must say per Bach that without reaching education one may feed him even by hand something forbidden — and Rama does not hold thus below siman 343.
machatzit-hashekel/part-001.txt.1:מ: (מ) And it appears to me the one who makes kiddush should have it in mind, etc. — meaning since Rama wrote there siman 273 per the Geonim it was permitted for the mohel and sandak to drink on Shabbat morning from the milah cup if they drink the required measure, but they practiced giving to the infant — end of his words; behold the custom is not to rely on the Geonim; and Rabbi Yosef Karo there in his long book was uncertain that perhaps Tosafot disagree with the Geonim; nevertheless the essence is as the Geonim. Nevertheless for advantage and counsel Magen Avraham wrote he should have in mind, etc., for some say one fulfills, etc. — Tosafot daf 105b wrote that in Yerushalmi it says: if one makes kiddush in one place and intends to eat in another place, this is called kiddush in the place of a meal. And Tosafot wrote: although in our Talmud it is proven there is no condition, one must say the Yerushalmi refers from room to room — sanctifying in one room on condition to eat in another room, but two rooms in one house the condition helps; but the Gemara refers from house to house — in such a case the condition does not help. But Ran wrote the language of Yerushalmi implies even from house to house the condition helps; if so the Yerushalmi disagrees with our Talmud and we rule like our Talmud — see there; at any rate per Ran the Yerushalmi holds even from house to house the condition helps although we do not rule like him; nevertheless one may make it a branch for what he drank a revi'it.

magen-avraham/part-001.txt.1:א: (א) They give a taste to a minor. Although it is forbidden to feed a minor a prohibition by hand as written siman 343 — that is regarding something that has a negative commandment; but kiddush is only a positive commandment (Hagah Maimoniyot in the name of Maharam). And per what is written in siman 343 that even a d'rabbanan prohibition does not apply to feeding by hand — one must say since some say even an adult may drink and fulfills through this kiddush, although we do not rule thus, nevertheless for minors it is permitted; or alternatively since it is a public need it is permitted [Beit Yosef]. And Bach wrote they give specifically to minors who have not reached education; but in responsum of Ran siman 82 in the name of Rashba that if one gives to such a minor it is a blessing in vain, for he has not reached education in blessing; and even in a place where they practice giving to the circumcised infant on the day of milah — that is because the blessing is for his sake; but in kiddush not — rather one must give to a minor who reached education. And per what Rabbi Yosef Karo wrote in siman 343 in the name of Rashba and Ran that in everything that is for the need of an infant such as eating and drinking, one may feed him by hand, for the Sages did not decree on it — for even in the synagogue there is a mitzvah to feed him and they do not educate him even for hours as written siman 326, all the more here. And there is a distinction between eating a prohibition and eating something permitted at a forbidden time, as Tosafot wrote Pesachim daf 106b; and all the more permitted to feed them on Shabbat morning before kiddush, for some say even an adult may eat as Raavad wrote — see there. And it appears to me it is forbidden to answer the minors, as written siman 326; and we are not concerned perhaps he will continue, for regarding something that is for the infant's correction they did not decree (Rashba in responsum siman 82 / 92). And that they give them a taste in kiddush and did not decree — because it is not a fixed matter, for sometimes there are guests and they do not give taste to the infant (Rashba siman 303): Hagah Maimoniyot wrote if there is no infant in the synagogue they give an adult to drink for kiddush and havdalah — end of his words. And it appears to me for kiddush he should drink the required measure as written siman 273 s.h. 5; and so Bach; and it appears to me the one who makes kiddush should have in mind to fulfill at his home through this kiddush, for some say one fulfills through this; and nevertheless he may sanctify again at home as written siman 273 s.d.

turei-zahav/part-001.txt.1:_: They are accustomed to make kiddush in the synagogue. Tur brings the words of Rav Natronai Gaon and wonders at them from the law; but in truth they are wondrous from the explanation of his language that is not correct; and a wide explanation is found on them: Beit Yosef explained they would make the first kiddush for healing and that was in the synagogue, and the second at home on account of kiddush in the place of a meal — and that is wondrous, for if so there is a blessing in vain, Heaven forbid; also regarding tasting that Rav Natronai wrote is for healing without specification and afterward wrote to place on their eyes; and furthermore at the start he did not bring proof that tasting is healing and afterward regarding eyes he brought proof from what we say one coarse step, etc. And in my humble opinion thus is the explanation of Rav Natronai Gaon's words: he explains that which we say kiddush is only in the place of a meal — the reason is not as Rashi brings in Beit Yosef that the Rabbis relied on the verse "call Shabbat delight" in a place of delight shall be the reading; rather on account of healing, for perhaps this was a tradition in his hand that the meal he makes after kiddush is healing for him, and therefore they agreed to kiddush for tasting — and that is the meal, as Tur wrote end of siman 273 in the name of the Geonim that drinking a cup is called in the place of a meal; found that there is no obligation of tasting on account of kiddush itself, for kiddush is without it and even without wine at all suffices by Torah law for kiddush as Tosafot chapter Ayin Peh daf 106 wrote — rather they relied together for healing. And the matter of kiddush in the synagogue of Rav Natronai Gaon was certainly that not all the congregation drank from the kiddush cup — that is a strange thing; and what he wrote that all the congregation taste — the explanation is not in the synagogue but rather all the congregation taste in their homes after kiddush on account of healing; and in the synagogue they did not drink, but perhaps one drank or they gave to an infant and the rest of the congregation placed on their eyes on account of healing as we say one coarse step, etc. And therefore here specifically proof is needed from above that he mentioned healing regarding tasting — he did not need proof that this is the essence of the explanation of kiddush in the place of a meal as written; rather here with placing on eyes and not drinking proof is needed that this too is healing; and the explanation of the matters is thus: although kiddush is only in the place of a meal, nevertheless they make kiddush in the synagogue, for the tasting of kiddush is not on account of the mitzvah of kiddush; and what all the congregation taste in their homes is on account of healing, not on account of the obligation of kiddush — for kiddush is fine without it, so it is in their homes; and this that he makes kiddush in the synagogue and gives to the congregation and they did not drink but only placed on their eyes — that too is for healing as stated on account of one coarse step, etc. And one may say: why place on the eye for healing — behold better the healing should be in their homes afterward through tasting; to this he answered: because there is one who has no wine and will not have this healing; therefore they enacted to make kiddush in the synagogue on wine and to place on their eyes — found both are in their hands: the mitzvah of kiddush although they did not taste, for the tasting is on account of healing; and here there is healing in what they place on the eyes as above. Correct is the explanation of Rav Natronai Gaon's words, and the difficulty of our teacher Tur is also resolved on them, with Heaven's help.
